policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Both readings are the same name with the same prefixed preposition, differing only in orthography: qere מִדָּֽנִיֵּ֑אל spells Daniel plene, ketiv מדנאל defectively without the yod. The ASV has 'thou art wiser than Daniel' and carries no note at this word; an English proper name plus 'than' renders either spelling identically, so nothing in the ASV distinguishes them. Underdetermined; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
